notice: RN bank batch 148: Pediatric case studies: ruptured appendix, scoliosis surgery, adolescent HEADSS visit and adolescent type 1 diabetes. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. questions.stem: Highlight the findings that suggest the appendix has ruptured.

cells: Sudden relief of pain, then worse

rationale.correct: Sudden pain relief followed by rigidity and fever means rupture with peritonitis.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: After laparoscopic appendectomy for a ruptured appendix, which parts of the plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Nothing by mouth for a week
Strict bed rest for the first few days

rationale.correct: Antibiotics, positioning, walking and abscess watch.

Treat the child like a toddler with a pacifier

caseStudies.title: Adolescent with type 1 diabetes missing insulin

exhibits.title: Diabetes clinic
exhibits.body: A 15-year-old with type 1 diabetes for 6 years has an HbA1c of 11.2% (was 7.4%). The teen has been skipping lunchtime insulin at school because friends ask questions. Today the teen has a stomach virus and vomited twice.

rows.label: Last basal insulin
cells: Skipped last night because "I wasn't eating"

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
